subject: QTL significant in scanone, but not in multiple QTL models

messages.author: 94bbbe52a1a2ee84
messages.subject: QTL significant in scanone, but not in multiple QTL models
parts:
Hi,

I am not sure how to interpret my finding for a minor QTL peak on linkage group 4 in the scanone, which is no longer significant after including covariates (composite interval mapping or multiple QTL model; see fig LODcurvesLG4.pdf). It seems to be that when added as a pair, the major QTL on LG2 cancels out the minor QTL on LG4 (see figure scantwo.pdf). This surprises me, as this is usually the case that after accounting for the variation associated with a major QTL, you will INCREASE the power to detect additional, small effect QTL. Here it seems to be reversed. The effect of these QTL is in the same direction (all QTL have effects in the same direction in this cross), so they are not repulsing QTL

Additional information of interest: this is a QTL scan in one of two mapping populations (families) of the same interspecies cross (n=94). The other family (n=136) has the same QTL on LG4 that is only significant in scanone, but not in multiple QTL models. Combining the two family-specific maps (n=230) and performing a QTL scan gives significant QTL on LG4 in both scanone and fitqtl output.

Figure legends: 

LODcurves show the LOD scores along LG4 from scanone (dashed line is 5% significance cut-off), CIM, and fitqtl after accounting for the effects from major QTL on LG1 and LG2 (significance thresholds for CIM and fitqtl are very close to the dashed line).

scantwo shows the increase in LOD score when adding two QTL as a pair allowing for epistasis (lower triangle) or only allowing for additive effects (upper triangle) relative to a single QTL model. Notice that QTL on LG1 and LG4 together approach significance, but that a pair of QTL on LG2 and LG4 does not. 

I would be interested to hear any suggestions as to how to interpret this result.

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] QTL significant in scanone, but not in multiple QTL models
parts:
Maybe look to see whether there is any genotype association between the locus on linkage group 2 and that on linkage group 4. That's the only thing that I can imagine is going on. And I'd trust the results after conditioning on the LG2 locus, over those from scanone.

karl

messages.author: 94bbbe52a1a2ee84
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] QTL significant in scanone, but not in multiple QTL models
parts:
Hi Karl, thanks for you feedback!

The association between the genotypes of marker on LG2 and those at the marker on LG4 is borderline significant, or not significant, depending on how you feel about p ~ 0.06 ;) But I take it this association (let's assume for the moment that it is there) is statistical and has no biological implication? Or could this under certain conditions imply linkage disequilibrium? I have alternative data which I can use to test that. 

The one thing that keeps bothering me, is that the LOD scores after correcting for the QTL on LG2 imply no linkage between the phenotype and LG4 in the two families, but the linkage in the full data set is strong enough to be considered significant (there is a QTL on LG4 in the multiple QTL model, albeit one that explains very little of the phenotypic difference between the parents). So say there is indeed a genotype association between LG2 and LG4, whether statistical or biological, would that simply reduce the power to detect an actual QTL on LG4 (therefore it is not present in the families separately, but it is in the full data set) or is the inferred QTL on LG4 in the full data set potentially a false positive?

best,

Thomas
